The petitioners have filed this petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/ for the death of Mr.Muddegowda in a road traffic accident dated 06.11.2021.
2.

The case of the Petitioners in brief is that, On 06.11.2021 at about 09.00pm the deceased Muddegowda was proceeding as a pillion rider in a TVS XL100 Heavy Duty moped bearing Reg.No.KA54Q5395, ridden by Vasudeva @ Balarama on BengaluruMangaluru NH75 Southern side Road at high speed in a rash and negligent manner.

When they reached near Devihalli Village Rice Mill, Bellur Hobli, Nagamangala Taluk, Mandya District, all of a sudden a Dog came across the Road in front of the moped, to avoid the Dog, the rider turned the moped to the side of the road at high speed, thereby he lost control over the vehicle and both fell down and suffered grievous head injuries.
3. It is the further case of the Petitioners that, soon after the accident, both were shifted to Aadichunchanagiri Hospital, B.G.Nagar and admitted as inpatients.
In spite of best efforts made by the doctors Muddegowda succumbed to the injuries at about 11.10pm on the same day.
After conducting the PM, the body was handed over to the family of the deceased.

The petitioners have Hucchamma Alias Sannathayamma vs Vasudeva C.P on 16 February, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59657543/
2 further claimed that they have spent Rs.1,25,000/ towards transportation and funeral obsequies.

sentences.text: They have claimed that the 1st petitioner is the wife of the deceased and petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the daughters of the deceased and they lost their loving husband and father.
Thereby all the petitioners are undergoing great mental shock, agony and financial loss.

At the time of accident, the deceased was aged about 64 years, hale and healthy and was doing Agriculture and Milk Vending business and earning more than Rs.25,000/ per month and contributing entire income for welfare and maintenance of the family.
The Jurisdictional Bellur police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the RVS XL100 Heavy Duty Moped bearing No.KA54A5395 p/u/Sec.279 & 304(a) of IPC.
The 1st respondent being the RC owner and the 2 nd respondent being the insurer of the said TVS XL100 moped are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners.
Hence, this petition.
4. In response to the summons issued by this court, the Respondents appeared through their respective counsels.
But the respondent No.2 alone filed written statement.
5. The objections of the Respondent No.2:
It has admitted the issuance of policy in respect of the TVS Excel 100 Heavy Duty bearing No.KA54Q5395.
It has claimed that the petition is not maintainable for non compliance of Sec.134(C) and 158(6) of the MV Act.
It has further contended that the vehicle is falsely implicated by the petitioner colluding with the owner of the vehicle and the police to get the compensation.
They have also contended that the rider of the TVS XL100 moped did not have a valid DL and after Investigation the charge sheet is filed under Sec.181 of MV Act.
Further contended that the rider was not wearing helmet as on the date of accident.

They have denied the age, occupation,
income and relationship of the petitioners with the deceased.
It has further contended that the compensation claimed by the petitioners is high, exorbitant.

Hence prays to dismiss the petition.
6.

On the above rival contentions of the parties, this court has framed the following issues:
1.
Whether the Petitioners prove that, they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sri.Muddegowda?

2. Whether the Petitioners prove that, Sri.Muddebowda died on account of road traffic accident took place on 06.11.2021 at about 9.00pm near Devihalli Village Rice Mill, Bellur Hobli, Nagamanagala Taluk, Mandya District, due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of TVS XL100 Heavy Duty bearing Reg.No.KA54Q5395?
3.
Whether the Petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?

4. What Order or Award?

My finding to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1 : In the affirmative Issue Nos.2 & 3: In the affirmative, Issue No.4 : As per final order for the Following:
REASONS 10. Issue No.1: In order to prove that the petitioners are the legal heirs of the deceased, the petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and has reiterated about the relationship in her affidavit in chief.
In addition she got marked the Aadhar cards of the petitioners and the deceased and the PAN Cards of the petitioners as per Exs.P.10 & 11.

In the Aadhar card of the petitioner No.1,
her husband's name is mentioned as Muddegowda.
However, the Aadhar cards of the petitioner Nos.2 to 6 mention their husband's name but in the PAN Cards of the petitioner Nos.2, 3 and 5, 6 their father's name is mentioned as Muddegowda.

Moreover in the inquest mahazar at Ex.P.5 also the wife's name is mentioned as Huchamma, his daughters' names are given as Dhanalakshmi,
Manjula, Sheela, Pushpalatha and Prathipa and is stated that all are married and they are living with their husband.
This shows that the petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the daughters of the deceased.
Accordingly, the Tribunal holds that the petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the daughters of the deceased.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is held in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Issue No.2:

The Petitioners, to prove that the accident occurred due to the actionable negligence on the part of the rider of the TVS moped have examined First Petitioner/Wife of the deceased as PW.1 and got marked Exs.P.1 to 9.

The contention of the respondent No.2 is that the rider of the TVS XL100 moped was not having DL to ride the vehicle as on the date of accident and after investigation the charge sheet is also filed u/Sec.181 of MV Act.
During the cross examination of PW.1, she has admitted that the rider did not have a valid DL as on the date of accident.
Her husband died due to head injury suffered in the accident.
Except this nothing is brought out to show the negligence of the deceased.
As per Ex.P.1 even though the accident occurred on 06.11.2021 at 21.00pm the complaint was registered on 07.11.2021 at 10.00am as per the complaint of the son inlaw of the deceased.
Thereafter as per Ex.P.3, 304(A) of IPC was also included in the charge sheet on the basis of the additional statement given by the complainant.
They have produced the sketch as per Ex.P.4 Therefore, there is nothing on record to show that the accident did not occur.

Moreover since the case is that the petitioner was a pillion rider, a Dog all of a sudden came across the road in front of the moped in which the deceased was a pillion rider, suddenly the rider turned his bike towards side of the Road, there is nothing to show any kind of negligence on the part of the deceased.
On the other hand, as per the records before the court the entire negligence is on the rider of the TVS XL100 moped.
Accordingly, on the basis of evidence of PW.1 and the documents on record, this Tribunal holds that the accident occurred due to the sole negligence on the part of TVS XL100 moped rider.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the affirmative.
12. Issue No. 3:
The petitioners have averred that the deceased was the sole bread earner of the family.
He was an Agriculturist and Milk Vendor and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/.
However in support of the same, PW.1 has neither examined anyone nor produced any documents.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon Civil Appeal No.6902/2021 : Kurvan Ansari alias Kurvan Ali and Anr. Vs. Shyam Kishore Murmu & Anr.
Wherein the Supreme Court of India has taken the notional income of a 7 year old at Rs.25,000/
per month.

sentences.text: However, this case cannot be applied to the case on hand since the deceased was 75 years old.
The accident occurred in the year 2021.
In the absence of any document, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,000/ per month .
Age of the deceased 13.
In so far as age of the deceased is concerned, the Petitioners have produced notarized copy of Aadhar Card of the deceased as per Ex.P.10.
This is a public document and has got presumptive value under law.
As per said document, the age of the deceased is 75 years as on the date of accident.
i) LOSS OF DEPENDENCY AND FUTURE  PROSPECTS:
As per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme court in National Insurance company Vs Pranay Sethi and others(AIR 2017 S.C 5157) persons aged above 60 years are not entitled to any future prospects.

The counsel for the petitioner has relied upon the decisions (2020) 11 Supeme Court Cases 356 : National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Birender & Ors.
Wherein it is observed that even earning sons of the deceased can apply for compensation and the Tribunal shall decide the quantum of compensation after deciding whether they were fully Dependant on the deceased or not.

sentences.text: In this case, the admission of PW.1 shows that the petitioner Nos.2 to 6 were not dependant on the deceased.
The deceased has a wife and married daughters.
In the cross examination of Pw.1, she has admitted that all the daughters are married and living with their husband.
It can be seen that the wife alone was depending on the income of the deceased.
Therefore, Pw.1 i.e., the petitioner No.1 wife is the only dependent of the deceased.

Since there is a sole dependent then 1/2 of the income has to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses,
balance comes to Rs.7,500/.

Therefore, the total loss of dependency would be Rs.4,50,000/
(Rs.7,500/ X 5 x 12 = Rs.4,50,000/).
ii) LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In Magma General Insurance company Limited Vs. Nanuram (2018)
18 SCC 130, the Hon'ble Apex court has observed "Consortium" is a compendious term, which encompasses spousal consortium, parental consortium and filial consortium.

sentences.text: The right to consortium would include the company, care, help, comfort, guidance, solace and affection of the deceased, which is a loss to her family.
With respect to a spouse, it would include sexual relations with the deceased spouse".

14. This observation of the Hon'ble Supreme Court is reaffirmed in United Indian Insurance Company Ltd. Vs. Satinder Kaur @ Satvinder Kaur and others, (2021) 11 SCC 780.
15.

sentences.text: The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and as she has lost her husband and companion at the age of 58 years and she has to the live remaining part of her life without him, she is entitled to a sum of Rs.44,000/ under the head of loss of consortium.
Similarly, the petitioner Nos.2 to 6 are the daughters of the deceased, they have lost their loving, care taking father.
Therefore, they are also entitled to Rs.44,000/ each, in total Rs.2,64,000/ (Rs.44,000/ x 6) is awarded under the head of loss of consortium.
iii) TRANSPORTATION AND FUNERAL EXPENSES:
PW.1/Petitioner has stated that she has spent Rs.3,00,000/ towards funeral expenses and obsequies etc..
In this regard the petitioner has not produced any bills pertaining to the above said expenses.
However, there are expenses during the death of a person for which documents cannot be maintained.
Therefore, in the interest of justice, the Petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/ under this head.
iv) LOSS OF ESTATE:
As mentioned above, the deceased was earning a sum of Rs.15,000/ per month.
Out of this, he was spending 1/2 of his income towards personal expenses.
Such being the case, out of this, certainly he would have saved some amount and created estate in favor of the Petitioners.
Therefore, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/ under the head of loss of estate.

As such, in total, the Petitioner is entitled to a sum of Rs.7,54,000/.
LIABILITY 16.
The Respondent No.2 has contended that the rider of the offending TVS XL100 moped did not have valid DL and was also not wearing the helmet at the time of accident.
The police have filed charge sheet against the rider of the TVS XL100 Heavy Duty Moped u/Sec.279, 337, 304(A) of IPC and Sec.181, 194(D) of MV Act.
Therefore, it can be held that there is breach of the terms of the contract by the owner/insured in riding the vehicle without possessing a valid DL and not wearing the helmet.
Therefore, the insurer i.e., the respondent No.2 is not under any liability to indemnify him.

The entire liability of paying the award amount is on the respondent No.1.
17.

Ltd. Vs. Swaran Singh.

sentences.text: To avoid its liability towards the insured, the insurer has to prove that the insured was guilty of negligence and failed to exercise reasonable care in the matter of fulfilling the condition of the policy regarding use of vehicles by a duly licensed driver or one who was not disqualified to drive at the relevant time".
Further the apex court has held that 'the Tribunal can direct the insurance company to pay the award amount to the claimants and inturn recover the same from the owner of the vehicle".

On the other hand The counsel for the Respondent No.2 has relied upon the decision in MFA No.6154/2019 (MVD) :

The chargesheet is also filed u/Sec.181 and 194(D) of the MV Act.
However the case of the petitioner is that the rider lost control of the bike when a Dog came across the Road infront of the moped.
This does not show absence of exercise of reasonable care on the part of the rider of the TVS moped.

18. Issue No.3:
For the reasons and discussions made above and findings to the above issues, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following: ORDER
The Petition filed by the Petitioners under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed with costs.

The Petitioners are entitled for Compensation of Rs.7,54,000/ (Rupees Seven Lakhs Fifty Four Thousand only) along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount and interest.
However, the Respondent No.2/Insurer is directed to deposit the compensation amount with interest before this Tribunal within sixty days from the date of this award.
Respondent No.2 is entitled to recover the award amount from the Respondent No.1.

On deposit of compensation and interest, Rs.2,00,000/ shall be deposited in the name of the petitioner No.1 in any N/S Bank for a period of 3 years, Rs.44,000/ each shall be released in the names of the petitioner No.2 to 6 and remaining amount shall be released in favour of the Petitioner No.1 by way of epayment on proper identification and due acknowledgment as per rules.
The Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1000/.
Draw Award accordingly.
